sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Personal Electronics and Smart Gadgets

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA, Chapter 10 Investment) — in force 31 October 2012
United Kingdom-Panama Agreement for the Promotion and Protection of Investments (1983) — in force 1985, applied bilaterally following Brexit
Canada-Panama Free Trade Agreement (Chapter 10 Investment) — in force 1 April 2013
Spain-Panama Agreement for the Reciprocal Promotion and Protection of Investments (1998)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 32 de 1927 (Ley General de Sociedades); Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2015 (AML/CFT framework); Ley 2 de 1 de febrero de 2011 (creates the Unidad de Análisis Financiero, UAF); Ley 70 de 2019 (AML amendments); Decreto Ejecutivo No. 53 de 21 de agosto de 2020 (mandatory Registro de Titulares de Derechos / UBO register for all legal persons); Acuerdo SBP No. 001-2016 (customer due diligence rules for regulated entities); and applicable FATF/GAFILAT recommendations as incorporated into Panamanian law.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Registro) of any foreign corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry in the shareholder's country of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency identifying directors and officers of foreign corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate service provider or registered agent of the foreign shareholder

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports and police clearance certificates (Certificado de Antecedentes Penales) of proposed shareholders, directors, and officers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country notary public and public prosecutor or designated issuing authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement for the initial contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or certified public accountant of the contributor

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening for all shareholders, directors, officers, and ultimate beneficial owners against the UAF domestic PEP and frozen-assets lists, OFAC SDN/SSI and Non-SDN lists, UN Security Council Consolidated List, and GAFILAT advisories. Screening is performed before engagement, upon any change in ownership or management, and continuously via automated refresh at least quarterly. A positive PEP hit, including a 12-month post-office cooling-off period, triggers enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification, senior management approval, and mandatory suspicious-transaction reporting to the UAF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá (www.registro-publico.gob.pa) — online name reservation and clearance module 'eRegistro' (Certificado de Nombre)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names may be registered in Spanish, English, or any other language using the Latin alphabet; non-Latin scripts must be transliterated to Latin characters in the constitutive deed. The name must carry a recognized corporate designator, including 'Sociedad Anónima', 'S.A.', 'Corporation', 'Corp.', 'Incorporated', 'Inc.', or 'Ltd.', and must be clearly distinguishable from all existing and reserved names in the Registro Público. Names that falsely imply government affiliation, regulated financial business, or a public institution are objectionable.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant receives a written refusal notice citing the conflicting registry entries. The applicant may, within five (5) business days of notification, file a 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the Dirección General del Registro Público, attaching a legal memorandum, an alternative name list, and evidence of prior use or trademark registration. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file a 'Recurso de Apelación' before the Sala Tercera de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within the statutory period. A fresh application with a distinct proposed name followed by expedited processing is also available.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual and administrative offices are permissible for the registered office of this non-regulated consumer-electronics e-commerce S.A., provided a licensed Panamanian resident agent maintains a physical address in Panama and accepts service of process. The entity must not rely solely on the virtual address when claiming Panamanian tax residency or territorial-source benefits; active Panamanian-source e-commerce income combined with an absence of local personnel or premises may attract economic-substance review under Ley 254 de 2021 and DGI administrative practice.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate: estimated unannounced on-site inspection probability of approximately 10% or less annually for a standard low-risk e-commerce entity; the probability increases to between 20% and 40% when UBO registry inconsistencies, sanctions or PEP alerts, tax arrears, or claims of tax residency without commensurate local substance are present.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and reservation certificate (Certificado de Nombre)
Drafting and notarization preparation of the Pacto Social and corporate bylaws
Notarial authentication of the incorporation deed (Escritura de Constitución)
Registration and inscription duty for the Sociedad Anónima (inscripción in the Registro Público)
Resident agent and registered office services — year 1
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark of USD 250–500 annually

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register filing (Registro de Titulares de Derechos) — initial declaration for all ultimate beneficial owners
Expedited processing surcharge (servicio urgente) for name clearance and registration

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: General Law on Corporations (Ley 32 de 1927), as amended by Ley 5 de 2007 and subsequent reforms; key provisions include Article 1 (formation), Article 14 (registration), Article 25 (share capital), Article 33 (registered office), and Articles 42-44 (directors and officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá (General Directorate of the Public Registry) – Corporation Registration Section
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Pública de Constitución (Public Deed of Incorporation) containing the Pacto Social y Estatutos
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required; the corporation must subscribe and issue at least one share with an arbitrary nominal value. There is no escrow account or capital deposit requirement. Share capital may be expressed in US dollars, the lawful currency of Panama.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the corporation has accepted subscription for the share capital listed in the Pacto Social, such subscription being fully paid as required by law. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the corporation shall be located at [insert address], Panama City, Republic of Panama, and that [Resident Agent Name] S.A. is appointed as resident agent under the Law. RESOLVED, that [Director 1], [Director 2], and [Director 3] are elected as the Board of Directors and that the Board appoints [Name] as President, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer for the initial term. RESOLVED, that the President and Secretary jointly are authorized to execute all incorporation filings, open bank accounts, and engage auditors. RESOLVED, that corporate books and seals be maintained at the registered office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – Name Reservation Section (Oficina de Registro de Nombres)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application electronically through the Public Registry's online platform or in person at the designated window. Provide up to three alternative corporate names. Pay the applicable name search fee and obtain a certificate of name availability.
required_dossiers: Completed name reservation application form
Photocopy of applicant's ID (cédula or passport)
Proposed corporate name (first, second, and third choices)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the chosen name is rejected for similarity or conflict, the applicant may file a revised name application with a new list of alternatives or appeal the registry's decision within five business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Public Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panama Notary Public (Notario Público) in Panama City
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before a licensed Panamanian notary for execution of the Escritura Pública de Constitución. The deed must include the Pacto Social (articles of incorporation), corporate purpose, share capital structure, registered office location, resident agent appointment, director names, and initial officers. Notarization is mandatory for full legal effect.
required_dossiers: Valid corporate name reservation certificate
Copy of passport or cédula of each incorporator
Certified translation of any non-Spanish supporting documents
Draft Pacto Social and Estatutos
Registered agent acceptance letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies omissions or inconsistencies, correct the deed and re-execute it on the same day; no additional governmental approval is required at this stage.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá – General Directorate of the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notarized Escritura Pública together with two certified copies at the Public Registry's headquarters. Pay the statutory registration fee and receive an entry number and receipt. The registry reviews the deed for formal legality, then records the corporation in the Mercantile Section.
required_dossiers: Notarized original of Escritura Pública de Constitución
Two certified copies of the public deed
Certificate of name reservation
Proof of payment of registration fees
Tax identification number (optional but recommended)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues an objection (razón de objeción), legal counsel must respond with a corrective amendment within 10 working days, or the filing will be deemed abandoned; re-file after curing the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Tax ID (RUC) and Municipal Operation Notice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Municipalidad de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the newly incorporated S.A. with the DGI through the online tax portal (Sedencia Electrónica) to obtain the Registro Único de Contribuyente (RUC). Subsequently apply to the local municipality for an Aviso de Operación, which permits the physical or virtual establishment to commence commercial operations.
required_dossiers: Certified copy (testimonio) of the registered Escritura Pública
Proof of appointment of legal representative
Copy of legal representative's ID
Proof of commercial address (lease or title deed)
Completed RUC application form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI rejects the RUC application for missing data, an administrative revision may be submitted within 15 business days; for municipal denials, appeal to the Alcalde's Office within five business days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá and Notary Public
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporate governance pack, including issuance of share certificates, stock ledger, meeting minutes book, and board resolution book. File any mandatory public registrations of officer changes, if applicable, and publish the notice of registered capital in a local newspaper only when the law so requires.
required_dossiers: Registry entry certificate proving public registration
Share subscription and payment records
Share certificate template and ledger
Minutes book and registry of directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If administrative fines arise for late filing of governance documents, request a remission or payment plan from the National Directorate of Revenue; for registry defects, file a clarification deed.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministerio de Comercio e Industrias (MICI) – Business Facilitation Directorate (no industrial manufacturing permit required for ISIC 4791 online retail activity)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación (Municipal Business Operation Notice) – the only mandatory operational permit for the e-commerce establishment

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE) – Department of Environmental Impact Assessment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not required for online retail of consumer electronics; Category N (Negligible) applies to warehouse/office use below 1,500 m2; a Category I Environmental Registration may be triggered if storage or logistics operations exceed the minimum area threshold.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC emission thresholds apply to e-commerce retail; waste handling must comply with Resolución No. 1314 de 2012 (hazardous waste, e-waste, batteries) and general non-hazardous solid waste disposal rules under Panama's national environmental code.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (Fire Department) for the office/warehouse; structural load inspection certified by a licensed engineer; workplace occupational health clearance from the Ministerio de Salud (MINSA) for any establishment, including e-commerce fulfillment areas, with sufficient employee count.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); official taxpayer portal: e-Tax 3.0 (https://etax.dgi.gob.pa; https://www.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Panama Sociedad Anónima must, through its resident registered agent, file the Aviso de Inscripción (DGI registration form) via the e-Tax portal within 30 days of incorporation at the Registro Público. The DGI issues the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente), which serves as the unified TIN and automatic ITBMS enrollment. Required documentary set: certificate of incorporation/public deed, registered agent appointment certificate, PAN/passport of directors and officer, proof of registered address in Panama, and opening balance sheet. Processing time is typically 3 to 10 business days; the RUC must appear on all invoices, customs declarations, and tax returns.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or entity pass-through election exists for a Panama S.A.; the sociedad anónima is taxed at the entity level on Panama-source income only. Available elections: (i) Pequeño Contribuyente simplified regime election for annual gross income up to PAB 36,000, substituting monthly ITBMS and advance income tax with a reduced annual gross-receipts tax; (ii) election to treat a Panama branch as a permanent establishment of the foreign head office; (iii) election to carry forward ITBMS input credits versus claiming a cash refund; (iv) accelerated depreciation election for qualifying electronic equipment; and (v) Multinational Headquarters (SEM) status under Law 41 of 2007, generally not applicable to pure e-commerce retail. Hybrid-mismatch elections are not recognized under Panamanian law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panama's VAT-equivalent on transfers of movable goods and provision of services)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Zero general de minimis threshold: any person or juridical entity, including a foreign-owned S.A., making taxable supplies of goods or services in Panama or importing goods must obtain the RUC and register for ITBMS with the DGI before commencing activities. An optional small-taxpayer threshold of PAB 36,000 annual gross income allows election of the simplified substitute regime in lieu of full ITBMS filing obligations.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama mandates electronic invoicing under the DGI Facturación Electrónica (FAS) system, phased in since 2022. Online retailers must issue e-invoices through DGI-certified billing software or the free e-Tax web/mobile FAS module, transmit invoice data in XML/JSON to the DGI in real time for fiscal clearance, and display the DGI-assigned QR code, digital stamp (Código de Registro FAS), and access key on each invoice. E-credit notes, e-debit notes, and electronic receipts follow the same prior-authorization framework. Domestic B2C and B2B sales require clearance; export invoices are covered by the zero-rating export evidence rules rather than local clearance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: An ITBMS 0% rate applies to (i) tangible goods physically exported from Panama by the seller, (ii) services rendered by a Panamanian taxpayer to a non-resident client for use entirely outside Panama, and (iii) qualifying free-zone and multitransit export transactions. An online consumer-electronics retailer can zero-rate cross-border sales only if the goods are shipped abroad, risk and title pass to the foreign customer at exit, and the export is evidenced by Panama customs documents. Domestic deliveries, free-zone deliveries for local consumption, and goods sold to tourists in Panama for local use remain subject to the 7% standard rate. The exporter must retain the full documentation bundle to substantiate the 0% rate and the corresponding input ITBMS credit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Panama SISCO / VUPE Declaración de Exportación)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical departure from Panamanian territory
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit voucher demonstrating receipt of export proceeds in a Panama-licensed bank
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI may retroactively audit export substantiation within the six-year tax prescription period. Incomplete or false evidence triggers reclassification of the supply as a taxable domestic sale, assessment of unpaid ITBMS at 7%, monthly late-payment interest at 1%, and fines ranging from PAB 500 to PAB 10,000 for invoice and customs documentation violations. Deliberate fraudulent zero-rating constitutes tax evasion (defraudación fiscal) under the Código Fiscal, punishable by imprisonment of 2 to 5 years, in addition to clawback of input ITBMS credits and surcharges of up to 100% of the tax evaded; foreign directors may be held jointly and severally liable for the assessed amounts.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Panama has no traditional central bank and the U.S. dollar serves as legal tender, with the Balboa pegged 1:1 solely as a fractional currency unit.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama is a fully dollarized jurisdiction with total capital and current account convertibility. There are no exchange controls, no central bank transfer approval, and no restriction on profit remittance. Dividends, royalties, and service payments may be freely transferred abroad subject only to documentary compliance by the bank and applicable tax filing requirements, not prior administrative authorization.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama does not impose any statutory timeline, mandatory conversion ratio, or surrender obligation on export receipts. Export proceeds in USD may be retained offshore or domestically in unrestricted amounts.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Trade Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility is Medium but restricted as a primary treasury rail. Panama permits supervised fintech payment processors, but foreign offshore EMIs cannot hold Panamanian corporate funds as a substitute for a SBP-licensed bank account. Such EMIs are acceptable only as settlement collection channels for retail e-commerce, subject to the underlying funds being swept to a local Panama bank account under explicit AML/CFT oversight.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for at least one director or the authorized legal representative when opening a corporate account for a Panamanian S.A., particularly for non-resident shareholders. Some banks permit remote opening via notarized corporate resolutions and video interviews for continuation account openings, but in-person interview at the branch remains the industry default under SBP due-diligence rules.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident or nominee shareholder structure with undisclosed beneficial ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current Ficha (corporate registry certificate), stock ledger and share deposit certificate, sworn beneficial ownership declaration, passport copies of the ultimate beneficial owner, notarized board resolution designating signatories, and source-of-funds explanation for the initial deposit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border e-commerce counterparties located in higher-risk jurisdictions or involving high transaction frequency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed commercial contracts, supplier invoices, logistics and courier tracking records, Stripe/PayPal payout summaries, completed bank reference letters from trading counterparties, and a written description of the customer-to-supplier payment flow.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid accumulation of retail card and wallet deposits disproportionate to expected revenue.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Monthly e-commerce platform settlement reports, reconciliation statements matching deposits to sales, external CPA attestation, VAT or income tax filings for prior months, and a clear organizational chart distinguishing commercial revenue from related-party transfers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of pooled payment processors or omnibus settlement accounts without beneficiary segregation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Processor sub-ledger showing individual customer purchases, daily sweep instructions to the Panamanian bank account, a compliance manual describing segregation and reconciliation of client funds, and an independent audit letter confirming no third-party payment obligations are commingled.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital contributions are routed via SWIFT MT103, referencing the company corporate stamp and investment purpose, using the Panama bank account and, where applicable, an intermediate U.S. correspondent bank via Fedwire or CHIPS. Panamanian banks do not require a statutory investment purpose code, but the remitter must provide a sworn source-of-funds statement and, when the contribution is paid against share issuance, a notarized capital subscription resolution must be lodged with the commercial registry.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements execute through outgoing SWIFT MT103 for open-account inventory purchases and through commercial letters of credit under UCP600 for larger, documentary-based import transactions. Domestic Balboa settlement is limited to local ACH; cross-border USD payments clear via Fedwire, CHIPS, or the correspondent banking network of the receiving country.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/PAB vanilla FX forwards (structurally unnecessary because of the 1:1 fixed peg)
USD versus major currency deliverable forward contracts
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on Latin American currencies for regional e-commerce receipts
Cross-currency interest rate swaps for trade finance and supply chain liquidity

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Sworn Income Tax Declaration (Declaración Jurada Anual de IR — Form 711 Informative Return where only foreign-source income exists / Form 722 Substantive Return where Panama-source income exists)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 March following the close of the calendar fiscal year (31 December); no filing fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fixed administrative fines (typically B/.100–B/.5,000) and monthly surcharges on any assessed tax; after 3 months of non-compliance the DGI may issue a presumptive tax assessment and initiate coactive (administrative collection) proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Flat Corporate Tax / 'Anualidad' (Franchise Tax for S.A. existence and registry good-standing; B/.300 annual fee for stated capital up to B/.10,000, B/.400 above that threshold)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) / Tesorería Nacional — collected through Banco Nacional and authorized corporate agents
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 April of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly late-payment surcharge (10% of the fee per commenced month) and official interest after 15 April; listing on the public 'delinquent' (en mora) registry; non-payment for 3 consecutive years triggers Treasury enforcement (juicio coactivo) and administrative cancellation of the corporate registration at the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial-Owner Declaration Update (Declaración Jurada de Beneficiario Final) — event-driven notarial declaration upon any share transfer or UBO change (no annual repeat filing if no ownership movement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Notary of the Republic of Panama; UBO records maintained with the licensed registered agent and produced to the Financial Intelligence Unit / DGI upon lawful request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after any direct or indirect share transfer or change in ultimate beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative AML penalties for late, inaccurate, or non-disclosed UBO information (fines up to B/.10,000); materially false declarations may be treated as a criminal money-laundering predicate offence.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No size-based or revenue-based compulsory audit applies to a private Panamanian S.A. engaged in online consumer-electronics retail (ISIC 4791). Mandatory independent audits attach only to banks, insurers/reinsurers, trust companies, securities issuers, and other regulated financial entities; an e-commerce S.A. without Panama-source income files the DGI informative declaration without audited financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by Panama (Junta Técnica de Contabilidad); qualifying non-public entities may apply the IFRS for SMEs standard. Internal books must be sufficient to support the annual tax/informative return, with book currency maintained in U.S. dollars (Panama being a fully dollarized economy).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Panama applies a custody-and-update model rather than an annual UBO attestation: the S.A. must (i) execute a notarized beneficial-owner declaration at incorporation, (ii) authenticate every share transfer by notarial deed and record transfers in the share-transfer ledger, and (iii) within 30 days of any transfer notify the licensed registered agent, who maintains the UBO file for inspection by the Financial Intelligence Unit. No separate annual UBO confirmation is filed when no ownership movement occurs; the paid annualidad receipt evidences continuing good standing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Directors (Registro de Directores, including alternates)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas — shareholders' and directors' minutes)
Share Transfer and Equitable Charges Ledger (Libro de Registro de Transferencia de Acciones y Gravámenes)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – USD 750 for a licensed Panama registered agent plus registered office address; average bundled renewal including the annualidad: USD 650 – USD 900
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: No statutory audit obligation; voluntary certified-audit engagement for an e-commerce S.A. typically ranges USD 3,000 – USD 6,500 per year, depending on transaction volume and payment-rail reporting

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat ISR (Impuesto sobre la Renta) on Panama-source taxable income, under Panama's territorial tax system (Código Fiscal, Title I, Chapter I).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to a standard Sociedad Anónima. The effective advantage is territoriality: sales to customers outside Panama, foreign fulfillment revenue, and income with no Panamanian situs are outside the taxable base, reducing the effective worldwide rate for cross-border e-commerce. Deductions include COGS, Stripe/PayPal merchant fees, transport/logistics, local warehousing, advertising, and salaries. No e-commerce-specific patent box or preferential rate is available for this consumer-gadgets retail S.A.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 140 (Declaración Jurada de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed through the DGI's Sistema T@X (tax administration portal; dgi.mef.gob.pa) using a registered Firma Digital/Apoderado. Accompanying schedules: financial statements certified by a licensed CPA for entities with annual gross revenue above B/. 3 million, transfer-pricing documentation, and the ESR annual return where applicable.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual declaration; quarterly mandatory advance payments of ISR (Form LE / Formulario 105) are due during the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual Form 140 must be filed within three months after the fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year S.A., the final deadline is March 31 of the following tax period. Payment must accompany the return. Extensions are not automatic; DGI may grant a written 1-month extension only upon justified application.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from Panama-source sales: invoiced value of consumer electronics and smart gadgets sold to clients physically located in Panama, before returns and discounts; gross-up for excise or direct taxes if withheld.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident online sellers without a Panama permanent establishment do not file Form 140 solely for distance sales. For the Panamanian S.A., include only Panama-situs sales; export sales to foreign customers should be excluded and recorded in the foreign-source income schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Returns, rebates, and discounts: contractual, documented reductions to gross sales actually granted in the tax period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only properly evidenced chargebacks/refunds issued through Stripe or PayPal and supported by sales ledger entries are deductible from gross revenue.
Should reconcile to the aggregate value of payment rails used in Panama from local customers; no offset against unrelated foreign receivables.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold: acquisition cost of smartphones, laptops, wearables and accessories sold, including shipping and customs duties actually incurred to bring inventory into Panama, determined under FIFO or average cost.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchases from a foreign related supplier must be supported by a transfer-pricing study and documented at arm's length.
If the S.A. acts as a low-risk distributor for a foreign related brand, gross margin should fall within the band tested under TNMM; atypical margins attract TP audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses: warehouse rent, local personnel salaries (reported on Form 110), Stripe/PayPal commission, affiliate marketing, IT infrastructure, depreciation, and support services. Expenses are deductible if necessary and properly documented.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Nominee or management-fee payments to offshore related parties are deductible only if the service is real, performed outside Panama, and evidenced by workpapers; marketing/administrative fees paid to a related BVI service company are presumptively challenged.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Add-backs and non-deductible disbursements: donations without authorization, personal expenses, penalties, taxes not instituted in Panama, bribes, and unsupported cash expenses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No add-back for foreign taxes on Panama-source income; foreign income taxes are not creditable, because Panama territorial law does not impose foreign income tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before loss carryforward (Box 405 minus Box 406 plus Box 407 adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: This is the benchmark for applying the TP local-file threshold and ESR substance indicators.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Less: tax losses previously declared and not expired, max 5-year carryforward period. Must be supported by an audited Form 140 for loss years.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident cannot use Panama losses against foreign-source income; losses are portable only to future Panama-source profits of the same legal entity.
Ensure not below zero; NOL cannot create a loss carryback in Panama.
No special solidarity surcharge applies; the statutory 25% is the final corporate rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits and withholdings against ISR: quarterly advance payments, source withholdings suffered, dividend WHT credits, and any banking tax paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident investors do not insert their shareholder data here; credits belong to the S.A. itself.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final ISR payable or credit balance: Box 411 minus Box 412.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If payment is financed by the foreign shareholder, a loan agreement at arm's length interest must exist; otherwise the balance is treated as constructive dividend subject to WHT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file Form 140 by the statutory deadline imposes a late-filing surcharge of 5% per month (or fraction) on the unpaid tax, capped at 50% of the tax due; interest is charged at the DGI's legal rate until paid. If no tax is due, a fixed administrative penalty of B/. 100 to B/. 1,000 applies. Materially false declarations constitute criminal tax fraud and expose the S.A. to fines of three times the evaded tax and imprisonment of two to six years for responsible managers; DGI may also seize bank accounts and domiciled assets without prior judicial order for listed fiscal debts.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 5% statutory withholding tax on dividends or profit distributions paid by a Panamanian S.A. out of Panama-source profits that have borne the 25% ISR; a 10% final withholding rate applies to distributions out of profits that were not taxed in Panama (territorial/exempt foreign-source income) unless the company has previously paid the 10% complementary dividend tax. A compliant electronics retail S.A. distributing audited locally-sourced profits will normally use the 5% rate and issue Form 150-D to the shareholder.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Panama has a narrow double tax treaty network, and treaty benefits are not available one-sidedly. To claim a reduced 0%-25% treaty rate on dividends/interest/royalties, the non-resident beneficial owner must: (i) obtain an official Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its residence country; (ii) submit a Form 160/DGI treaty-benefit declaration attaching the TRC and conduit-ownership affidavit; (iii) file with the Dirección General de Ingresos for a prior administrative confirmation (acuerdo de reciprocidad); and (iv) deliver the approved documentation to the paying S.A. before the distribution or payment date. The S.A. must withhold the statutory rate until the DGI approves the reduced rate, and must retain the TRC/ruling for five years. If the treaty is not in force because no PAN-foreign DTA exists, no reduction applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties for the use of trademarks, software copyrights, patents, or know-how in Panama paid to a non-resident are subject to a 12.5% statutory withholding tax, reducible only under an applicable treaty after the TRC protocol above is satisfied. Interest: pure interest paid by the Panamanian S.A. to a foreign bank or non-related lender with no Panama situs is 0% withholding tax under territorial sourcing; interest paid on shareholder debt or to a related foreign lender is subject to anti-avoidance review and may be recharacterized as a distribution subject to the 5/10% dividend WHT if excessive or not documented. There is no 30% debt-equity safe harbour in Panama's code for general e-commerce companies; thin-capitalization rules are enforced through substance and arm's length norms.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Local File/Formulario 170-TP is triggered when consolidated related-party transactions (cross-border or domestic) exceed USD/B/. 250,000 in a fiscal year; if the Panamanian entity's annual gross income exceeds USD/B/. 3 million, TP documentation is also required regardless of transaction value. Master File must be prepared when the ultimate parent's global consolidated revenue exceeds USD/B/. 20 million. Filing and penalties follow the OECD-aligned Decree 63/2016 rules; these thresholds are in Balboas (PAB), the legal currency pegged 1:1 to the United States dollar.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama Law 70 of 2019 and Executive Decree 286 of 2019 impose explicit economic substance requirements on an S.A. that performs any "relevant activity," which includes distribution, logistics, service provision, financing, and IP holding. The present online retail of consumer electronics and smart gadgets is a distribution/relevant activity, so the S.A. must maintain: a filing address and real office/warehouse facilities in Panama; full-time qualified employees (admin, logistics, compliance) proportionate to volume; board and operational decisions made in Panama; local bank accounts in Panama that support invoicing; and annual ESR reporting to the DGI. The use of exclusive nominee directors, virtual-only operations, or foreign outsourced fulfillment without local control will trigger a denial of substance. The doctrine also applies to a "pure equity-holding" parent of the retail subsidiary; a definitive waiver is available only for truly dormant companies whose sole assets are shares and that file the negative ESR affirmation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Knowingly filing Form 140 with lower Panama-source sales than the Stripe/PayPal/Mastercard settlement records, overstating COGS with fake invoices, using personal/proxy payment gateways to hide local fulfillment, or paying no ISR for three consecutive years with repeated operational losses despite sustained e-commerce volume.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Panama's tax code and Penal Code punish the evasion with a penalty of three times the evaded tax, plus late-payment surcharge and interest; the responsible natural person may be sentenced to 2-6 years of imprisonment, with a warrant of embargo on corporate bank accounts and competing commercial credit lines. DGI may administratively close the fiscal registration and issue a certificate of insolvency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the S.A. as a nominal invoicing shell: no Panamanian employees, no warehouse, no local leadership, board meetings mail-only, registered agent nod-off, and no ESR report filed while claiming distribution revenue for related-party transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of Law 70/Decree 286 exposes the company to an annual economic substance failure penalty of USD/B/. 10,000 up to USD/B/. 1,000,000 or 0.5% of gross income if higher; the DGI may refuse to issue or renew the operation's Aviso de Operación, nullify tax receipts, and apply for judicial dissolution of the S.A. as a fictitious entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Nominee directors who certify false substance reports may be personally fined and banned from acting as director in Panama; directors may be subject to restitution of the penalties if they knowingly used a shell to evade ESR and TP rules. Travel bans per Ley 40 may be imposed for unpaid fiscal penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Related-party transactions above the USD/B/. 250,000 threshold without a contemporaneous Local File, TP policies detached from economic contribution, excessive management/allocation fees paid to a BVI/Oman/Ireland related services affiliate, or a year-end margin below 1% while the group retains 20%-30% in foreign co-contractors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DGI will adjust taxable income to the arm's length standard, assess the 25% ISR difference, impose an additional penalty of 10%-30% of the adjustment, add unpaid-amount interest, and apply a late-filing sanction of at least B/. 1,000. If the TP documentation is fabricated, criminal liability for fraud follows; a final administrative determination may be published in official registries and attached to the S.A.'s compliance file.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the CFO cannot shield behind the corporate entity when they sign inaccurate Form 170-TP; Panama courts may pierce the veil, hold individuals jointly and severally for the additional tax, and order precautionary embargo of personal assets, passports and exit permits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / Money Laundering through Payment Rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting Stripe/PayPal funds in Panama without registering as a regulated e-money service provider, transacting in physical delivery with unknown customers in high-risk jurisdictions, receiving structured cash deposits split under USD/B/. 10,000 to avoid reporting, processing sanctioned-country credit cards, or laundering tax-evaded corporate profits through personal accounts of the beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Panama Law 23 of 2015 and the AML Criminal Code, a juridical person may be fined up to USD/B/. 1,000,000 per violation; a license or operating permit may be revoked, and financial institutions may terminate correspondent banking. Criminal prosecution for money laundering carries 5-12 years of imprisonment for the natural-person operators and sequestration of assets used in the predicate offense.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Senior management may be charged criminally without requiring a prior corporate conviction; civil seizure of personal property, travel bans under Código Procesal Penal, and disqualification from future directorship in Panama are the standard consequences.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring Panama-source profits abroad to the sole foreign shareholder as "repayment of shareholder loan," "foreign service fee," or "software licensing charge" without withholding the 5% dividend tax, distributing declared dividends after the annual shareholders' meeting but failing to pay Form 150-D, or booking a dividend in foreign currency in an offshore PayPal account not registered with the S.A.'s Panama tax books.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The S.A. is personally liable for the unpaid 5% or 10% dividend withholding tax, plus the late-filing surcharge of 5% per month (cap 50%) and statutory interest; DGI may order an embargo of the S.A.'s receivable bank accounts, levy on inventory, and impose a fixed fine for failure to issue withholding forms. In egregious cases, the amount is also gravamen for fraud since the administration is the unpaid creditor.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: In Panama, directors who are responsible for distributing dividends without making the tax retention act as de facto statutory withholding agents and may be jointly and severally liable for the withheld tax, with additional personal fines and an exit-bar travel restriction until the debt is paid.
